title: K-flat preservation and quasi-isomorphism inversion after point evaluation
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme whose category of module sheaves [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure] admits a derived category. Put $A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and let $p:X\to (\mathrm{pt},A)$ be the global sections ringed-space morphism [def-pc-global-derived-rhom]. Let $e:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{pt}})\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(A)$ be an equivalence whose forward functor is naturally isomorphic to evaluation. Let $P:\operatorname{Mod}(A)\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ be additive, strong monoidal, and a left adjoint. Assume its object and morphism formulas are exactly inverse evaluation followed by inverse image and change of rings along the adjoint structure map of $p$ [lem-pc-kflat-pullback-preservation]. Then its termwise homotopy functor $P^h$ sends every K-flat object [def-pc-kflat-complex] to a K-flat object. Moreover, for a quasi-isomorphism $a:K\to M$ between K-flat homotopy objects, $Q_X^h(P^h(a))$ is an isomorphism. No flatness or boundedness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Cohomology Lemma pullback-K-flat and the quasi-isomorphism argument in derived-base-change, after the one-point identification of Tag 0B6A

proof.text: Evaluation at the unique nonempty open commutes with the sheaf tensor and its coproduct totalization. The isomorphism he therefore identifies e with the canonical exact monoidal evaluation equivalence. Its inverse preserves acyclicity and K-flatness: test the tensor against an acyclic complex, move it through the equivalence, and use the inverse unit/counit. This also identifies the generic quasi-isomorphism-preservation definition of K-flatness with the acyclic-tensor definition used for sheaves.

The formulas h and hm identify termwise P, including its differentials, with inverse evaluation followed by the concrete ringed-space tensor pullback. The inverse-image/tensor-pullback comparison and the identity-ring-map case of K-flat pullback preservation show that exact inverse image preserves K-flatness. Applying K-flat pullback preservation to toGlobalSectionsPoint X gives the first assertion after passing to the homotopy quotient.

Lift a homotopy morphism between K-flat complexes to a cochain morphism using fullness of the quotient. Exact inverse evaluation and exact module inverse image preserve its quasi-isomorphism. Change of rings preserves the resulting quasi-isomorphism between K-flat inverse-image complexes. Transport by h and hm and use the quotient quasi-isomorphism criterion; Qh inverts the resulting morphism, proving the second assertion.
